verses.english: Middle Discourses 120
Rebirth by Choice
So I have heard.

verses.pali: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,
“Mendicants!”
“Venerable sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:
“I shall teach you rebirth by choice.

verses.pali: taṁ suṇātha, sādhukaṁ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti.
verses.english: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

verses.pali: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
verses.english: “Yes, sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:

verses.pali: “Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saddhāya samannāgato hoti, sīlena samannāgato hoti, sutena samannāgato hoti, cāgena samannāgato hoti, paññāya samannāgato hoti.
verses.english: “Take a mendicant who has faith, ethics, learning, generosity, and wisdom.
They think:

verses.pali: ‘aho vatāhaṁ kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā khattiyamahāsālānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjeyyan’ti.
verses.english: ‘If only, when my body breaks up, after death, I would be reborn in the company of well-to-do aristocrats!’

verses.pali: So taṁ cittaṁ dahati, taṁ cittaṁ adhiṭṭhāti, taṁ cittaṁ bhāveti.
verses.english: They settle on that thought, stabilize it, and develop it.

verses.pali: Tassa te saṅkhārā ca vihārā ca evaṁ bhāvitā evaṁ bahulīkatā tatrupapattiyā saṁvattanti.
verses.english: Those choices and meditations of theirs, developed and cultivated like this, lead to rebirth there.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, maggo ayaṁ paṭipadā tatrupapattiyā saṁvattati.
verses.english: This is the path and the practice that leads to rebirth there.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saddhāya samannāgato hoti, sīlena samannāgato hoti, sutena samannāgato hoti, cāgena samannāgato hoti, paññāya samannāgato hoti.
verses.english: Furthermore, take a mendicant who has faith, ethics, learning, generosity, and wisdom.
They think:

verses.pali: ‘aho vatāhaṁ kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā brāhmaṇamahāsālānaṁ …pe…
verses.english: ‘If only, when my body breaks up, after death, I would be reborn in the company of well-to-do brahmins …
well-to-do householders.’

verses.pali: So taṁ cittaṁ dahati, taṁ cittaṁ adhiṭṭhāti, taṁ cittaṁ bhāveti.
verses.english: They settle on that thought, stabilize it, and develop it.

verses.pali: Tassa te saṅkhārā ca vihārā ca evaṁ bhāvitā evaṁ bahulīkatā tatrupapattiyā saṁvattanti.
verses.english: Those choices and meditations of theirs, developed and cultivated like this, lead to rebirth there.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, maggo ayaṁ paṭipadā tatrupapattiyā saṁvattati.
verses.english: This is the path and the practice that leads to rebirth there.

verses.english: Furthermore, take a mendicant who has faith, ethics, learning, generosity, and wisdom.
And they’ve heard:
‘The gods of the four great kings are long-lived, beautiful, and very happy.’
They think:

verses.pali: ‘aho vatāhaṁ kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā cātumahārājikānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjeyyan’ti.
verses.english: ‘If only, when my body breaks up, after death, I would be reborn in the company of the gods of the four great kings!’

verses.pali: So taṁ cittaṁ dahati, taṁ cittaṁ adhiṭṭhāti, taṁ cittaṁ bhāveti.
verses.english: They settle on that thought, stabilize it, and develop it.

verses.english: Those choices and meditations of theirs, developed and cultivated like this, lead to rebirth there.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, maggo ayaṁ paṭipadā tatrupapattiyā saṁvattati.
verses.english: This is the path and the practice that leads to rebirth there.

verses.english: Furthermore, take a mendicant who has faith, ethics, learning, generosity, and wisdom.
And they’ve heard:
‘The gods of the thirty-three …
the gods of Yama …
the joyful gods …
the gods who love to create …
the gods who control what is created by others are long-lived, beautiful, and very happy.’
They think:

verses.pali: ‘aho vatāhaṁ kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā paranimmitavasavattīnaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjeyyan’ti.
verses.english: ‘If only, when my body breaks up, after death, I would be reborn in the company of the gods who control what is created by others!’

verses.pali: So taṁ cittaṁ dahati, taṁ cittaṁ adhiṭṭhāti, taṁ cittaṁ bhāveti.
verses.english: They settle on that thought, stabilize it, and develop it.

And they’ve heard:
‘The Divinity of a thousand is long-lived, beautiful, and very happy.’

verses.pali: Sahasso, bhikkhave, brahmā sahassilokadhātuṁ pharitvā adhimuccitvā viharati.
verses.english: Now the Divinity of a thousand meditates focused on pervading a thousandfold galaxy,

verses.pali: Yepi tattha sattā upapannā tepi pharitvā adhimuccitvā viharati.
verses.english: as well as the sentient beings reborn there.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, cakkhumā puriso ekaṁ āmaṇḍaṁ hatthe karitvā paccavekkheyya;
verses.english: As a person with clear eyes might pick up a gallnut in their hand and examine it,

the Divinity of three thousand …

verses.english: Now the Divinity of ten thousand meditates focused on pervading a ten-thousandfold galaxy,

verses.english: Suppose there was a beryl gem that was naturally lustrous, eight-faceted, well-worked. When placed on a cream rug it would shine and glow and radiate.

the gods of streaming radiance …

the gods of Aviha …

the gods fair to see …

the gods of Akaniṭṭha …

verses.english: ‘If only I might realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom in this very life, and live having realized it with my own insight due to the ending of defilements.’

verses.pali: So āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati.
verses.english: They realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom in this very life. And they live having realized it with their own insight due to the ending of defilements.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na katthaci upapajjatī”ti.
verses.english: And, mendicants, that mendicant is not reborn anywhere.”
That is what the Buddha said.

verses.pali: Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṁ abhinandunti.
verses.english: Satisfied, the mendicants approved what the Buddha said.
